recipes.name: Macaroni and Tomatoes
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.5 ounce) can chopped stewed tomatoes, with juice
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Once the water is boiling, stir in the macaroni, and return to a boil. Cook the pasta uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the pasta has cooked through, but is still firm to the bite, about 8 minutes. Drain well in a colander set in the sink.

Pour the macaroni into a saucepan and place over medium heat; stir in the butter, bacon grease, tomato sauce, stewed tomatoes with juice, and sugar; season with salt and pepper. Stir while cooking until butter and bacon grease has melted and incorporated completely, 5 to 10 minutes; remove from heat, cover, and allow to sit about 20 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Macaroni and Tomatoes
raw_recipe.description: This is a delicious side dish to add to about anything.

review.reviewBody: I started out making this when I was really super broke and the only meat I could afford was bacon. It always increases easily with what you have on hand and however many people you have to feed. I make this now for my boys and add in bacon, add a little bit of spice and toss with parmesan cheese. Never fails to get smiles!

I made this at my hubby's request. I have not eaten this dish before so I went on his description of how his dad used to make it as to how this was supposed to be. This turned out wonderfully and my husband was well pleased. He said it was exactly like his dad's were except he wanted it soupier, so the next time I will add some tomato juice instead of sauce or maybe in addition to. I didn't have bacon grease, I just doubled the butter. Thanks for sharing this, it brought my hubby some warm fuzzies as he has some great memories of his dad. Plain and simple, this is good comfort food!

My husband requested "tomato mac" like his mother used to make, I couldn't get ahold of her so I found this recipe hoping he would have liked it. This turned out okay and it wasn't anything impressive. I'm not a big fan of noodle dishes to begin with anyhow. I did finally get ahold of my mother-in-law and her recipe was so much more simple and so few ingredients I thought surely it was just going to taste worse than this one. I was so so wrong. All it required was butter to your liking (we use about half a stick or so) per one big box of dry macaroni, a diced onion, and one can of diced tomatoes. You melt the butter, soften the onions, throw the macaroni in as well as the can of diced tomatoes and one can of water. The BIG BIG difference I think in her recipe is that she tosses her macaroni in dry and then stirs it all well, throws the lid on and turns the heat completely off after bringing it up to a boil and lets the pasta sit and absorb all the tomato juices and butter.

I was surprised to see this recipe. My mother use to make this when I was little. It has always been a comfort food to me!! She just used the macaroni and a can of tomatoes.....salt and pepper and you are good to go! Its even great cold....my adult kids make it and take camping as a cold side dish. Now the grand kids even like it. 4 generations!!!!!!

THANK YOU for sharing this! I was scrolling through looking for a new macaroni dish when I saw it. This is one of those all time favorites that I grew up with, and now my kids make it for their families.

My version is only slightly different. I use the bacon grease & butter to sweat half a diced onion before adding everything together, and I always use petite diced tomatoes instead of stewed. (as a kid I hated all the little bits of celery & stuff in the stewed ones). If using diced instead of stewed...use a pinch more sugar.

Thanks again for sharing this!
this recipe is my hubbys favorite...I did use 2 cans of rotel tomatoes instead of stewed tomatoes to add that extra kick!!

I'm so glad i discovered this! As a poor college kid, I'm always excited to find cheap, yummy recipes, and this is definitely one of those!! So easy. I used extra butter instead of bacon grease, and added some garlic salt and Parmesan cheese. Will definitely make this over and over again!

Wow I thought we were the only ones who ate this...lol My husband won't even try it...but growing up in PA, my mom would use elbow macaroni, a jar of her home canned tomatoes, little butter, and pepper (salt was already in tomatoes) and I loved it! I make it frequently for myself, however...I never had it with bacon grease in until now...this version is very good...I think bacon flavor makes everything good...but I'll probably stick to my mom's version because I like just the taste of the tomatoes...thank you for the great recipe!

I grew up eating this, but not as a side dish, as main course dinner. Mostly, a fair amount of crisp bacon was mixed in, but occasionally, browned ground beef, sausage or leftover chicken was added. I’d recommend that you do use “stewed” tomatoes, they add real sweetness. If this is of any help, I used my kitchen shears right in the can to chop the stewed tomatoes. I did add a just a couple slices of crisp bacon as well as some crushed red pepper flakes (personal taste). Sure, there are many options on variations to this mac and tomatoes, but there are times when simple is best, and we certainly enjoyed this as written. Another plus for this dish is that it’s extremely budget-friendly.

Loved this! Followed JMac' suggestions for the most part. Need to make sure the onion is fully cooked before adding the pasta in the future. Had 2 half-bags of pasta to use up: some elbow mac and some chile paprika penne so used it all. Used a can of Italian-style diced tomatoes, a can of water, a half can of marinara sauce and another half can of water. Let it sit for about 15 minutes to soak up the sauce. Hubby loved! He added some shredded cheese to his but I opted to skip those extra calories. Did need a little salt. So easy and good! Will definitely make again.

I grew up eating macaroni and tomatoes at least weekly. I could never get mine to taste like my mom's- until this recipe. My only thing different- she always put onions in it too, and never sugar. I sauted my onions in the butter and bacon grease before tossing in everything else. Perfect comfort food, with my pinto beans and cornbread on a snowy day.

This is exactly how my grandmother made this, except she used tomato juice to wash out the can after adding the tomatoes instead of the tomato sauce. Sometimes if we were lucky she would crumble up any bacon left from breakfast that day. We always had cornbread made with White Lily cornmeal mix and baked in a cast iron skillet (NO SUGAR in it please!) with plenty of butter! Thanks for the memories!

I grew up eating this and if you leave out the bacon grease, it will not, let me say that again, IT WILL NOT taste the same. I do not put sugar in mine. I always fry up fresh bacon and use what ever bacon greese is left and set the bacon aside for sandwiches later. I then add the onion and canned tomatoes, salt and pepper and let that simmer on the lowest heat while cooking the large elbow macaroni in another pot until almost done. Drain the elbow macaroni and stir into the tomatoes and let simmer for about 10 minutes until you see the elbow taking on the red color. Serve
So tasty! I love it!
Had to add a little more sugar but other then that it was Great..Thank you I will be making this again
Very easy very good
Used only fresh tomatoes and threw in garlic onion green pepper and some three cheese blend yum
Followed to the T, Love it, have had many times with salmon cakes, just like my moms tasted years ago
Perfectly balanced. Great side dish and easy. It has the right amt of sweetness and tomatoes.

What a wonderful memory brought back to my taste buds. I loved it. I altered it a wee bit by blanching about 5 tomatoes and removing the outer layer( peelings) I then chopped them up and placed them in the pan with 2 cups of macaroni along with the other ingredients. I added just a touch more bacon grease and it was lovely..... followed directions as stated and it turned out just right Thank you??????
